coverageNote: Enumerated 10 units / 58 files from disk — exactly matches the expected 10 units, 58 files. Every unit is a directory containing an *-index.md: the domain root (index, cx, and three domain-level leaf features 19.10/19.11/19.12) plus nine sub-domain folders 19.01-19.09. All 58 files were read. Normative sections (Overview, Role Lens/Role Matrix, Behavior, Happy Path, Edge Cases, States, Decisions, Open Questions, Cross-Cut Map + Cross-Cut Details, Rejected Pairs) were read at full fidelity in every file. In the later units (19.03 onward) the 'Deep Think Annotations' justification prose and the auto-generated 'Cross-Cut Notes' / 'Related Specs' link lists were read in reduced form (DT rows truncated to hypothesis + verdict) to fit the ~957 KB tree into context; DT verdicts were cross-checked against the corresponding Decisions rows in every case, and every DT-derived decision is restated in the Decisions table, so no normative content was skipped. Structural checks (index/cx presence, Role Matrix population, Role Lens presence, status markers, PENDING marker census, deferral-target census, invariant/formula grep) were run programmatically across all 58 files.
rubricNote: Applicable dimensions per unit: 1 (Problem Clarity, via each unit's Overview), 2 (Persona Specificity, via Role Matrix / Role Lens), 3 (Feature Completeness), 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability, via the units' numeric thresholds), 7 (Open Question Resolution), 8 (Structural Compliance). Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) is N/A throughout — it belongs to meta/competitive-landscape.md, not to a domain or feature file. 7 applicable checkpoints x 10 units = 70; 7.5 points = 10.7% ambiguity.

structuralSummary.classificationGateViolations: none — no folder with a single child; the three flat domain-level features (19.10/19.11/19.12) each carry a single capability

findings.claim: The canonical count (19.05.01) has no `carted` counter and defines `remaining` without subtracting it, while the manifest invariant it is supposed to report on (19.01.02 D-06) makes `carted` a bucket disjoint from `remaining`. The two definitions of `remaining` cannot both hold during a live on-sale, and `remaining` is what the storefront reads as its availability boolean.
findings.evidence: 19.05.01-live-count-manifest-state.md:36 — "| **Remaining** | Sellable right now (= capacity − killed − held − paid − comp) | The storefront (as a boolean to Fans) |". No `carted` row exists anywhere in the counter table (lines 28-36) and the string 'carted' does not appear in 19.05.01 at all. Against 19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:34 — "licensed capacity  =  killed + held + comp + paid + carted + remaining" — and 19.01.02:43 — "| `carted` | Reserved to a buyer mid-checkout (`19.02.04`) | Cart hold create/expire |" — and 19.01.02:44 — "| `remaining` | Sellable right now | Derived — never written directly |". 19.01.02 is itself internally split on the same point: 19.01.02:122 — "Operator sees a lower available figure than `remaining` during on-sale, with carted quantity stated" — and 19.01.02:154 — "Available-to-hold shown separately from `remaining` because `carted` is untouchable" — both of which only make sense if `carted` is inside `remaining`, contradicting D-06's disjoint identity at 19.01.02:214.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent (a) whether the canonical count carries a `carted` counter at all, (b) whether `remaining` is net or gross of in-flight carts, and (c) whether available-to-hold equals `remaining` or `remaining − carted`. Choosing 'gross of carts' makes the storefront's availability boolean show units that are already reserved (oversell exposure on the last units of an on-sale); choosing 'net' contradicts 19.01.02's own available-to-hold gloss. 19.05.01 D-01 explicitly forbids consumers computing their own count, so this cannot be resolved locally by a consumer.
findings.notAMarkerCase: No `[PENDING]`, `[OWNER]`, `[DEFERRED]` or open question on either statement. 19.05.01's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 cover minimum disclosure, single-party certification and the blended-source boundary — none touches `carted`. 19.01.02's Q-01..Q-09 do not either.

findings.claim: The all-in headline price formula includes an amortised per-order fee term, while D-05 and DT-05 of the same file forbid amortising per-order fees into per-ticket lines. Because the headline is a per-price-level (per-ticket) figure quoted at first impression, when the order size is not yet known, the amortisation denominator is undefined.
findings.evidence:
19.01.03-fee-structure-all-in-pricing.md:34-37 — "all_in(tier) = face_value
             + Σ(per-ticket mandatory fees, each rounded at its own line)
             + amortised per-order mandatory fees        [see per-order handling below]
             + tax(on the taxable base for the jurisdiction)". Against 19.01.03:116 — "| D-05 | Per-order fees remain order-scoped for settlement and refunds, never amortised into per-ticket lines | Amortising corrupts settlement attribution and refund math (DT-05) |" — and 19.01.03:92 (DT-05) whose Source column is the display argument itself: "| DT-05 | Per-order fees should be spread evenly across tickets so every line shows one blended per-ticket price | Display-simplicity argument — one number per ticket reads cleanly | ❌ REJECTED — amortising a per-order fee into per-ticket lines corrupts settlement ... Per-order fees are disclosed at order level in the headline math but remain a distinct order-scoped line for settlement and refund correctness. |". The prose at 19.01.03:40 restates the order-scoping — "Per-order fees (a single handling charge, delivery) apply once per order, not per ticket ... the buyer sees the per-order component itemised at cart before commit" — without reconciling it with the 'amortised' term in the formula.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the headline composition for a regulated first-impression price: (a) face + per-ticket fees only, with the per-order fee disclosed at cart; (b) face + per-ticket fees + the whole per-order fee (a 1-ticket assumption); or (c) face + per-ticket fees + per-order-fee ÷ some assumed quantity. All three produce different legally-mandated headline numbers for the same inventory, and D-02's display/charge invariant ("the all-in total shown at first impression is the exact total charged") binds whichever is chosen. 19.01.03 Q-01 (RESOLVED — US only, residual = which named US instruments sit inside the headline) covers *which components* are in scope, not *how a per-order component is expressed in a per-ticket headline*.
findings.notAMarkerCase: The formula line carries a bare cross-reference ("[see per-order handling below]"), not a tracking marker. No open question in 19.01.03 (Q-01 jurisdiction, Q-02 platform fee, Q-03 mid-sale increase legality, Q-04 price-guarantee on decreases) covers the amortisation mechanic.

findings.claim: 19.11 RSVP states that the capacity cap counts heads rather than RSVPs (so one RSVP may be several heads) and simultaneously that every admission is a real scannable record keyed to the RSVPing Fan's identity, one head per person. How a party RSVP produces admission records for the accompanying heads — and what a one-tap self-release returns — is unspecified.
findings.evidence: 19.11-rsvp-free-private-event-admission.md:56 — "| Someone RSVPs for 6 | Free events attract inflated party sizes | Cap counts heads, not RSVPs (D-05) |" and 19.11:116 — "| D-05 | The cap counts heads, not RSVPs | Free events attract inflated party sizes |". Against 19.11:113 — "| D-02 | RSVP issues a real admission record that scans, counts and closes like a ticket | A name on a list with no scannable artifact is the same failure as a comp with no barcode (19.03.02 DT-01) |" — 19.11:54 — "| RSVP with no admission record issued | A name on a list with no scannable artifact | Same failure as a comp without a barcode (19.03.02 DT-01) — the record must be real |" — and 19.11:93 (DT-03) — "the admission record is keyed to the Fan's identity (D-11: fans are real users, not CRM rows), so a repeat RSVP resolves to the same record rather than a new head against the cap" — plus 19.11:117 (D-06) — "RSVP is idempotent per Fan and self-releasable — one head per person, one-tap 'can't make it' returns the seat".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent: (a) whether a party of 6 mints 6 admission records or 1 record admitting 6 (D-02 requires a real scannable artifact per admitted body; DT-03 keys the record to the RSVPing Fan's identity, and the other 5 are people the platform knows nothing about); (b) how a 6-head record interacts with 19.04.01's use-once barcode and D-09 3-second debounce at the door; (c) whether the one-tap self-release returns 1 seat or all 6, and whether partial release exists. The directly analogous problem is settled explicitly for guest lists — 19.03.01:117 D-05: "An allocation counts **admission units** (one body, one barcode); a `+1` spends a unit and issues its own ticket; entry spend is atomic (no partial spend)" — and 19.11 has no equivalent rule.
findings.notAMarkerCase: No marker on any of the statements. 19.11's four open questions are Q-01 deliberate overbooking, Q-02 venue-less events, Q-03 domain-07 boundary, Q-04 free-becomes-ticketed conversion — none covers party size or record cardinality.

findings.evidence: ticketing-box-office-index.md:49 — "**Cross-cuts**: [ticketing-box-office-cx.md](./ticketing-box-office-cx.md) — 14 intra-domain pairs, 6 rejected pairs, 8 cross-cut mechanisms routed out, and the domain's 3 characteristic mechanisms." The CX file actually carries 21 cross-cut entries (ticketing-box-office-cx.md:12-32, CX-01 through CX-21), 7 rejected pairs (ticketing-box-office-cx.md:396-402, R-01 through R-07), and 10 routed-out mechanisms (ticketing-box-office-cx.md:379-388: Payments, Chargebacks, Fraud engine, Consent, Age assurance, Tax, Notifications, Attestation, Holds/reservation lifecycle, Health-adjacent access-requirements PII). findings.claim: 19.01.04's Behavior section asserts that seat maps are a domain-16 room asset; the same file's own Q-01 records that this assertion is wrong and that domain 16 explicitly declines to hold seat identities and map geometry. The erroneous statement is left unmarked in the normative section, and the reconciliation is owned by a question in another domain.
findings.evidence: 19.01.04-seating-model-ga-reserved-seat-maps.md:31 — "Seat maps are a room asset (domain 16) reused across shows; the show selects a *configuration* of the room, and the manifest is instantiated from it." Against 19.01.04:94 (Q-01, marked RESOLVED) — "**Collision recorded, not resolved**: the same DT-04 declines seat identities and map geometry — *\"The room does **not** carry **seat identities or map geometry** ... Both domains are pointing at each other\"* — so this file's assertion that *\"seat maps are a room asset (domain 16)\"* is wrong, and the reconciliation is tracked as `16.01.02` Q-02." The same wrong premise propagates into Happy Path step 1 (19.01.04:35 — "Operator selects the show's room; system offers the room's saved configurations") and Edge Cases (19.01.04:51 — "| Seat map missing for a room | Reserved/Mixed models unavailable ... Operator sees a CTA to build the map (domain 16)"). Corroborated as a real ownership gap by 19.01.05:118 (Q-02) — "16 declines seat identities and map geometry (`16.01.02` D-05), so per-**position** accessible identities are 19's to hold".
findings.notAMarkerCase: The Behavior, Happy Path and Edge Case statements carry no `[PENDING]`/`[OWNER]` marker; only the closed Open Questions table records the contradiction, and the reconciliation it names (`16.01.02` Q-02) sits outside domain 19, so nothing in this unit will correct the normative text.

findings.claim: 19.04.04's Behavior and Happy Path state that the show's age restriction is sourced from the room's licence in domain 16, while the same file's Q-04 establishes that domain 16 carries no audience age restriction at all and that the restriction is therefore Operator-declared per show. The normative text is left unamended and unmarked.
findings.evidence: 19.04.04-door-age-id-verification.md:27 — "A show carries an age restriction sourced from the room's licence (domain 16) and adjustable upward by the Operator for a specific show." and 19.04.04:35 (Happy Path step 1) — "Room's licence (domain 16) supplies the default age restriction; Operator confirms or raises it for this show." Against 19.04.04:115 (Q-04, marked RESOLVED) — "**RESOLVED — neither: 16 carries no audience age restriction at all.** `16.01.06` **D-06** locks the set: *\"**Five statutory slots, locked**: occupancy ceiling · liability cover · electrical/fire-safety record · performing-rights licence status · hirer requirements\"* — an audience age restriction is not among them ... **There is therefore no upstream default to inherit, and the restriction is Operator-declared per show here.**" The domain index corroborates the gap at ticketing-box-office-index.md:110 (Q-12 point 3) — "**Licensed age restriction** — **no**: D-72's US profile locks exactly five statutory slots ... and an age restriction is not among them, so `19.04.04` Q-04's requirement currently lands on nobody."
findings.notAMarkerCase: No marker on the Behavior or Happy Path statements. An implementer following Happy Path step 1 would build an inheritance from a domain-16 field that does not exist; the correction lives only in a table row marked resolved further down the file.

findings.claim: Transfer of an accessible ticket is listed as an edge case whose behaviour is a bare `[PENDING]` with no owner and no deferral target, and no open question anywhere in the tree covers it — despite accessible tickets carrying a companion entitlement whose door behaviour is a hard cross-cut requirement.
findings.evidence: 19.09.02-ticket-transfer-delivery-controls.md:58 — "| Transfer of an accessible ticket | The accessible position may not suit the recipient | `[PENDING]` |". No owner, no target. 19.09.02's four open questions cover holding decrement (Q-01), rotating delivery (Q-02), notification addressee (Q-03) and chain visibility (Q-04) — none reaches it; 19.01.05's four (jurisdiction, domain-16 modelling, companion entitlement number, on-sale block) do not either. The unresolved behaviour is load-bearing: 19.01.05:110 (D-05) binds a zero-fee companion entitlement to the position — "An accessible position and its entitled companion(s) are one order carrying exactly one per-order fee" — and ticketing-box-office-cx.md:26 (CX-15) makes the pairing a door rule — "the companion must scan **with** the position holder at the same lane, not independently — the door needs the companion-to-position link from the config". 19.01.05:54 also confirms transfer/resale of accessible inventory is an anticipated live path — "any resale of an accessible ticket is flagged to domain 24".
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether a transferred accessible position (a) carries its companion entitlement to the recipient, (b) voids the companion ticket, (c) returns the position to the accessible block and re-offers it, or (d) transfers like any other ticket. Each yields different door behaviour under CX-15's same-lane pairing rule and different fee arithmetic under 19.01.05 D-05's single-per-order-fee parity guarantee.
findings.notAMarkerCase: Bare `[PENDING]` — no owner, no deferral target — and unlike the other bare `[PENDING]` markers in this tree (19.02.04:48, 19.02.05:49, 19.04.04:51, 19.08.01:60, 19.08.02:45/:49/:52, 19.08.03:58/:60, 19.09.03:53), which each map to a properly owned Open Question row, this one is uncovered.

notableStrengths: Every unit has index + cx; every index has a populated Role Matrix; every leaf carries a Role Lens. No Classification Gate violations.

Prior contradictions have been explicitly remediated with owner decisions and the superseded rule retained for history — 19.04.02 D-06 marked "SUPERSEDED by D-11" (DQ-16.3/16.4/16.5/16.6) resolving a drifted duplicate rule between 19.04.01 D-06 and 19.04.02 D-06; and 19.05.01 D-09/D-10/D-11 (DQ-17.1/17.2/17.3) splitting `scanned` (gate) from `admitted` (window) with `admissions_total` derived, propagated into 19.03.02 D-02, 19.05.04 D-13, 19.07.03 D-07 and ticketing-box-office-cx.md CX-04's explicit correction note.

Normative thresholds are numeric and testable throughout: 60-minute amber staleness with per-show override (19.04.02 D-11), 120s clock-skew band (19.04.02 D-07), 72h counter-attestation / discretionary-case deadlines (19.05.05 D-07, 19.06.01 D-07), 3-second scan debounce (19.04.01 D-09), `remaining ≤ max(10% of sellable, 20 units)` held-inventory alert (19.01.02), 10 000 bp fee-split sum and round-half-up at the fee line (19.01.03 D-04), ±10% face-value sanity check (19.07.04 D-06).
Owner-only product decisions are consistently isolated with `[OWNER]` + a named next stage, and resolved questions cite the ratifying decision verbatim rather than asserting closure.
